facts.text: After the coronation, Shivaji Maharaj accomplished 'Dakshin Digvijay', the conquest of the South.
facts.quote: After the coronation, Maharaj accomplished 'Dakshin Digvijay', the conquest of the South.

facts.text: The Swaraj comprised large areas of Nashik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur, Sindhudurg, Ratnagiri, Raigad and Thane districts, and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: The Swaraj expanded comprising large areas of Nashik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur, Sindhudurg, Ratnagiri, Raigad and Thane districts of Maharashtra. It also included parts Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu States.

facts.text: At the time of his coronation, Shivaji Maharaj appointed the Ashtapradhan Mandal, a council of eight ministers.
facts.quote: Ashtapradhan Mandal (Council of Eight Ministers) : At the time of his coronation, Shivaji Maharaj appointed a council of eight ministers.

facts.text: The administration was divided into eight departments; the eight Heads of department made up the Ashtapradhan Mandal.
facts.quote: The administration was divided into eight departments. A Head was appointed for each department. These eight Heads of department constituted the Ashtapradhan Mandal.

facts.text: Maharaj alone could appoint or remove a minister; the ministers were answerable to him.
facts.quote: Maharaj alone had the power to appoint a minister or to remove him from his position. The ministers were answerable to Maharaj

facts.text: The Council was selected on merit; members got no jagirs, vatans, gifts or fiefs but were paid handsome salaries.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj selected the Council on the basis of their merit and achievements. He did not give them jagirs, vatans or gifts or fiefs. They were paid handsome salaries instead.

facts.text: Moro Trimbak Pingle was the Pradhan: running the administration and making arrangements for the conquered territories.
facts.quote: Moro Trimbak Pingle | Pradhan | Running the administration and making arrangements for the conquered territories

facts.text: Ramchandra Nilkanth Muzumdar was the Amatya: keeping the accounts of the State.
facts.quote: Ramchandra Nilkanth Muzumdar | Amatya | Keeping the accounts of the State

facts.text: Annaji Datto was the Sachiv: preparing royal edicts.
facts.quote: Annaji Datto | Sachiv | Preparing royal edicts

facts.text: Dattaji Trimbak Waknis was the Mantri: correspondence.
facts.quote: Dattaji Trimbak Waknis | Mantri | Correspondence

facts.text: Hambirrao Mohite was the Senapati: organisation of the Army and protection of the kingdom.
facts.quote: Hambirrao Mohite | Senapati | Organisation of the Army and protection of the kingdom

facts.text: Ramchandra Trimbak Dabir was the Sumant: foreign relations.
facts.quote: Ramchandra Trimbak Dabir | Sumant | Foreign relations

facts.text: Niraji Rawaji was the Nyayadhish: dispensing justice.
facts.quote: Niraji Rawaji | Nyayadhish | Dispensing justice

facts.text: Moreshwar Panditrao was the Panditrao: looking after religious matters.
facts.quote: Moreshwar Panditrao | Panditrao | Looking after religious matters

facts.text: Maharaj entrusted the organizing of the land revenue system to his capable and experienced office bearer Annaji Datto.
facts.quote: He entrusted the responsibility of organizing the land revenue system to his capable and experienced office bearer Annaji Datto.

facts.text: Officers were warned not to collect more revenue than the fixed amount; peasants were encouraged to bring uncultivated land under cultivation.
facts.quote: He warned the officers that they should not collect more revenue than the amount that was fixed. He encouraged peasants to bring uncultivated land under cultivation.

facts.text: If crops were lost due to excessive rains or drought, or an enemy army devastated a village, remissions were granted in land revenue and other taxes.
facts.quote: If the crop was lost due to excessive rains or drought, or if an enemy army had devasted the area of the village, remissions were granted in land revenue and other taxes.

facts.text: Officers were instructed to provide peasants with bullocks, ploughs and good seeds for sowing.
facts.quote: Maharaj had instructed his officers to provide peasants with bullocks, ploughs and good seeds for sowing.

facts.text: Baluta was the definite share of their produce that farmers gave to artisans; the village was a self-sufficient unit.
facts.quote: In this sense, a village was a self-sufficient unit. Farmers gave a definite share from their produce to artisans. This share was called 'Baluta'.

facts.text: The Ajnyapatra describes merchants as 'the ornaments of the kingdom and the glory of the king'.
facts.quote: the Ajnyapatra where merchants are described as follows: 'Merchants are the ornaments of the kingdom and the glory of the king.'

facts.text: Maharaj protected the salt industry in Konkan by charging heavy duty on salt imported from the Portuguese territory.
facts.quote: He protected the salt industry in Konkan. ... Maharaj charged heavy duty on the salt imported into Swaraj from the Portuguese territory.

facts.text: The army of Shivaji Maharaj had two main divisions: infantry and cavalry.
facts.quote: There were two main divisions of the army of Shivaji Maharaj : infantry and cavalry.

facts.text: The infantry had officers such as the Havaldar and Jumledar; its chief, the highest officer, was called Sarnobat.
facts.quote: In the infantry there were officers such as the Havaldar, Jumledar, etc. The chief of the infantry was called Sarnobat. He was the highest officer in the infantry.

facts.text: In the cavalry, a Shiledar had his own horse and weapons; a bargir was given a horse and weapons by the State; bargirs were more in number.
facts.quote: The Shiledar had his own horse and weapons. The bargir was provided with a horse and weapons by the State. In the cavalry, bargirs were more in number.

facts.text: The highest officer in the cavalry was the Sarnobat; Netoji Palkar, Prataprao Gujar and Hambirrao Mohite were famous Sarnobats.
facts.quote: The highest officer in the cavalry was the Sarnobat. Netoji Palkar, Prataprao Gujar, Hambirrao Mohite were some of the famous Sarnobats of the cavalry.

facts.text: Bahirji Naik was the Head of the intelligence department; he collected information about Surat before the raid on Surat.
facts.quote: Bahirji Naik was the Head of the intelligence department. ... He collected accurate and detailed information about Surat before the raid on Surat.

facts.text: The Ajnyapatra says: 'This kingdom was created by the late revered and exalted Majesty forts alone.'
facts.quote: The importance of forts in the foundation of Swaraj is well stated in the Ajnyapatra : 'This kingdom was created by the late revered and exalted Majesty forts alone.'

facts.text: 'Budhabhusanam', composed by Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, describes the forts built from Karnataka up to Baglan, from the river Krishna up to the sea, and mentions the Rayari fort.
facts.quote: the treatise 'Budhabhusanam' composed by Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj ... in many places from Karnataka up to Baglan ... from the banks of the river Krishna up to the sea ... In the Rayari fort

facts.text: There were about 300 forts in the Swaraj.
facts.quote: There were about 300 forts in the Swaraj.

facts.text: Maharaj built hill forts like Pratapgad, Pavangad and Rajgad.
facts.quote: He built hill forts like Pratapgad, Pavangad and Rajgad.

facts.text: Every fort had a Killedar, a Sabnis and a Karkhanis; the Karkhanis looked after the storage of foodgrains and the maintenance of war material.
facts.quote: There was a Killedar, a Sabnis and a Karkhanis on every fort. The Karkhanis looked after the storage of foodgrains and the maintenance of war material on the fort.

facts.text: Maharaj built the sea fort Sindhudurga at Malwan; five khandis of lead were poured into its foundation.
facts.quote: One of the sea forts that he built was Sindhudurga at Malwan. It is an excellent sea fort. To give strength to the construction of the fort, five khandis of lead was poured into its foundation.

facts.text: The sea fort Padmadurga was built in front of Rajapuri to counter the Siddi power: 'another Rajapuri to overshadow the Rajapuri of the Siddi'.
facts.quote: A sea fort called Padmadurga was built in front of Rajapuri in order to counter the Siddi power. ... 'another Rajapuri to overshadow the Rajapuri of the Siddi.'

facts.text: The Portuguese of Goa, the Siddi of Janjira and the British factors of Surat and Rajapur created obstacles on the west coast.
facts.quote: Enemies on the west coast of India, the Portuguese of Goa, the Siddi of Janjira and the British factors of Surat and Rajapur, created obstacles in the work of expanding the Swaraj.

facts.text: To protect the west coast Maharaj raised a navy; he realised that the one who has a navy controls the sea.
facts.quote: For this purpose, Maharaj raised a navy. He realised that the one who has a navy, controls the sea

facts.text: The navy had four hundred ships, including battle ships like the gurab, galbat and pal.
facts.quote: There were four hundred ships of various kinds in his navy. They included battle ships like the gurab, galbat and pal.

facts.text: Ships were built in the creek of Kalyan Bhivandi, Vijaydurga and Malvan.
facts.quote: Ships were built in the creek of Kalyan Bhivandi, Vijaydurga and Malvan

facts.text: Maynak Bhandari and Daulatkhan were the chief naval Commanders.
facts.quote: Maynak Bhandari and Daulatkhan were the chief naval Commanders.

facts.text: The main objective of Maharaj was to make his subjects independent, with a disciplined administration that cared for people's welfare.
facts.quote: His main objective was to make his subjects independent. ... it was necessary to have a disciplined administration, take comprehensive care of people's welfare and protect the conquered territories.

facts.text: Forts let rulers watch the surrounding area, shelter people during invasion, and stock foodgrains, war materials, ammunition and a garrison.
facts.quote: Possession of a fort made it possible to keep an eye on the surrounding area. In case of foreign invasion it was possible to protect the people taking shelter in the fort. It was possible to stock the fort with foodgrains, war materials, ammunition and military garrison.

facts.text: The salt duty was meant to make imported salt cost more, so its import would fall and the sale of local salt would rise.
facts.quote: The intention was that the salt imported from the Portuguese territory would then cost more and as a result, its import would decrease and the sale of the local salt would increase.
